    • GHOST AWS Deployment and Operations Requirements

    UID: GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-OPERATIONS
    VERSION: 0.4

    1. 1. Scope, Evidence, and Environment Profile

    STATEMENT: This document refines the runtime-platform parent with atomic requirements for the documented current AWS deployment, the approved target remote MCP extension, and the approved target serverless EC2 runtime-control extension.

    CURRENT means documented deployed behavior. TARGET means required future behavior that is not yet implementation truth.
    GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY
    1.1. AWS Deployment and Operations Capability
    UID: GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-RUN-OPS-CAPABILITY AWS Runtime Platform and Operations Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-SET Deployment Evidence Set
    • GHOST-AWS-CURRENT-TARGET-LABELING Current and Target Requirement Labeling
    • GHOST-AWS-LOCAL-PROFILE-CONTRACT Local Deployment Profile Contract
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-BASE-IMAGE CURRENT Docker Base Image
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-ECR-IMAGE CURRENT Private ECR Image
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-START-SCRIPT CURRENT EC2 Startup Script
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-PUBLIC-ENDPOINT-CHECK CURRENT Public Endpoint Verification
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-PHASE1-NONGOALS CURRENT Phase-1 Non-Goals
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-MCP-SAME-EC2 TARGET MCP on Existing EC2
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: GHOST shall reproduce the documented current Phase-1 AWS deployment and shall add the target remote MCP deployment and target serverless EC2 runtime-control deployment without changing the current Streamlit service unless a TARGET requirement explicitly requires an additive change.
    GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-SET
    1.2. Deployment Evidence Set
    UID: GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-SET
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY AWS Deployment and Operations Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-CONFLICT-VISIBILITY Deployment Evidence Conflict Visibility
    STATEMENT: CURRENT requirements shall be derived from the supplied AWS deployment guide, supplied HTTPS reverse-proxy architecture, supplied ragstream-start script, and current repository deployment artifacts.

    TARGET MCP requirements shall be derived from the approved deployment decisions and the applicable MCP, Claude, and ChatGPT interoperability specifications.

    TARGET EC2 runtime-control requirements shall be derived from the approved GHOST operating decisions documented for remote start, stop, status, selectable instance profile, readiness verification, and inactivity shutdown.
    GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-CONFLICT-VISIBILITY
    1.3. Deployment Evidence Conflict Visibility
    UID: GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-CONFLICT-VISIBILITY
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-EVIDENCE-SET Deployment Evidence Set
    STATEMENT: When supplied narrative documentation and a supplied executable deployment artifact describe different concrete commands, the requirement set shall preserve both facts explicitly and shall identify the executable command as the current executed configuration rather than silently rewriting either source.
    GHOST-AWS-CURRENT-TARGET-LABELING
    1.4. Current and Target Requirement Labeling
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CURRENT-TARGET-LABELING
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY AWS Deployment and Operations Capability
    STATEMENT: Every deployment requirement shall be identifiable from its UID and title as either CURRENT or TARGET, and no TARGET MCP behavior shall be represented as already deployed.
    GHOST-AWS-LOCAL-PROFILE-CONTRACT
    1.5. Local Deployment Profile Contract
    UID: GHOST-AWS-LOCAL-PROFILE-CONTRACT
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY AWS Deployment and Operations Capability
    STATEMENT: Exact account identifiers, region, hostnames, resource identifiers, paths, commands, current configuration text, and target implementation-assigned values shall be recorded in 81_aws_deployment_profile.local.md.

    Secret values shall not appear in either requirement file or the local profile.

    2. 2. CURRENT AWS Network and HTTPS Entry

    STATEMENT: The current public path is Route53 -> EC2 public IPv4 -> Security Group -> nginx -> local Docker-published Streamlit backend.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST
    2.1. CURRENT EC2 Host
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY AWS Deployment and Operations Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-ROOT-VOLUME CURRENT EC2 Root Volume Capacity
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST-SOFTWARE CURRENT EC2 Host Software
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-A-RECORD CURRENT Route53 A Record
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-WEB-PORTS CURRENT Public Web Ports
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-SSH-RESTRICTION CURRENT SSH Source Restriction
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-NGINX-WEB-ENTRY CURRENT nginx Web Entry
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-ROLE-PERMISSIONS CURRENT EC2 Role Permissions
    STATEMENT: The current deployment shall run on one Ubuntu 24.04 EC2 instance in a public subnet with a public IPv4 address and an attached IAM instance profile.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-ROOT-VOLUME
    2.2. CURRENT EC2 Root Volume Capacity
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-ROOT-VOLUME
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    STATEMENT: The current EC2 instance shall use a root EBS volume with at least 20 GiB capacity.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST-SOFTWARE
    2.3. CURRENT EC2 Host Software
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST-SOFTWARE
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    STATEMENT: The current EC2 host shall have Docker, AWS CLI, nginx, and Certbot installed, and Docker and nginx shall be enabled for the documented deployment operation.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-A-RECORD
    2.4. CURRENT Route53 A Record
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-A-RECORD
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-IMDSV2-IP-READ CURRENT IMDSv2 Public-IP Read
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-UPSERT CURRENT Route53 Address Update
    STATEMENT: The configured Route53 A record shall resolve ragstream.rusbehabtahi.com to the current EC2 public IPv4 address using the configured TTL.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-IMDSV2-IP-READ
    2.5. CURRENT IMDSv2 Public-IP Read
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-IMDSV2-IP-READ
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-A-RECORD CURRENT Route53 A Record
    STATEMENT: The current startup script shall obtain an IMDSv2 token and shall use that token to read the EC2 public IPv4 address from instance metadata.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-UPSERT
    2.6. CURRENT Route53 Address Update
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-UPSERT
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-ROUTE53-A-RECORD CURRENT Route53 A Record
    STATEMENT: The current startup script shall UPSERT the configured Route53 A record with the public IPv4 address read from IMDSv2 during each successful activation.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-WEB-PORTS
    2.7. CURRENT Public Web Ports
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-WEB-PORTS
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-NO-8501 CURRENT No Public Streamlit Backend Port
    STATEMENT: The EC2 Security Group shall allow public inbound TCP traffic on ports 80 and 443 for the documented web entry path.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-SSH-RESTRICTION
    2.8. CURRENT SSH Source Restriction
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-SSH-RESTRICTION
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    STATEMENT: Inbound TCP port 22 shall be restricted to the trusted administrator source and shall not be open to all internet addresses.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-NO-8501
    2.9. CURRENT No Public Streamlit Backend Port
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-NO-8501
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-SG-WEB-PORTS CURRENT Public Web Ports
    STATEMENT: The EC2 Security Group shall contain no public inbound rule for TCP port 8501.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-NGINX-WEB-ENTRY
    2.10. CURRENT nginx Web Entry
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-NGINX-WEB-ENTRY
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-EC2-HOST CURRENT EC2 Host
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-TLS-TERMINATION CURRENT TLS Termination
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY CURRENT Streamlit Reverse Proxy
    STATEMENT: nginx on the EC2 host shall be the intended public web entry point and shall select the application server block for ragstream.rusbehabtahi.com.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-TLS-TERMINATION
    2.11. CURRENT TLS Termination
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-TLS-TERMINATION
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-NGINX-WEB-ENTRY CURRENT nginx Web Entry
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-HTTP-REDIRECT CURRENT HTTP-to-HTTPS Redirect
    STATEMENT: nginx shall terminate TLS for ragstream.rusbehabtahi.com using the Let's Encrypt certificate managed by Certbot.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-HTTP-REDIRECT
    2.12. CURRENT HTTP-to-HTTPS Redirect
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-HTTP-REDIRECT
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-TLS-TERMINATION CURRENT TLS Termination
    STATEMENT: Requests received on public port 80 shall be redirected to HTTPS on port 443 under the Certbot-managed nginx configuration.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY
    2.13. CURRENT Streamlit Reverse Proxy
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-NGINX-WEB-ENTRY CURRENT nginx Web Entry
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY-TIMEOUT CURRENT Streamlit Proxy Read Timeout
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-8501-PUBLISH CURRENT Docker Host Port 8501 Publication
    STATEMENT: The nginx application route shall proxy to http://127.0.0.1:8501 using HTTP/1.1 and shall preserve the Host, X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, Upgrade, and Connection headers required by the supplied configuration.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY-TIMEOUT
    2.14. CURRENT Streamlit Proxy Read Timeout
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY-TIMEOUT
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY CURRENT Streamlit Reverse Proxy
    STATEMENT: The current Streamlit nginx route shall use the documented long proxy read timeout so long-running Streamlit connections are not terminated by the reverse proxy.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-8501-PUBLISH
    2.15. CURRENT Docker Host Port 8501 Publication
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-8501-PUBLISH
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-STREAMLIT-PROXY CURRENT Streamlit Reverse Proxy
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-8501-PROTECTION-COMBINATION CURRENT Port 8501 Protection Combination
    STATEMENT: The current startup script shall publish host port 8501 to container port 8501 with Docker -p 8501:8501, which binds host port 8501 on all host interfaces.
    GHOST-AWS-CUR-8501-PROTECTION-COMBINATION
    2.16. CURRENT Port 8501 Protection Combination
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-8501-PROTECTION-COMBINATION
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-8501-PUBLISH CURRENT Docker Host Port 8501 Publication
    STATEMENT: Direct public access to the broadly published host port 8501 shall be prevented by the Security Group prohibition on public inbound port 8501, while users access Streamlit through nginx on HTTPS port 443.

    3. 3. CURRENT Docker Image and ECR Delivery

    STATEMENT: The current repository builds one Streamlit image and pushes it to the configured private ECR repository. Image activation on EC2 remains a separate step.

    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):

    3.5. CURRENT Repository Copy
    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-COPY

    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKER-STREAMLIT-CMD
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):

    STATEMENT: The current image shall set PYTHONPATH=/app and STREAMLIT_SERVER_PORT=8501, expose container port 8501, and start ragstream/app/ui_streamlit.py with Streamlit listening on 0.0.0.0:8501.

    UID: GHOST-AWS-CUR-DOCKERIGNORE-RUNTIME-DATA
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):

    9. 9. TARGET MCP Tool and Existing-Code Boundary

    STATEMENT: This section defines only the deployment-facing boundary for MCP tools and their existing-code dependencies. Common MCP protocol behavior remains owned by 110_mcp.sdoc. Prompt Engineering and non-ActiveBlackboard memory capabilities remain owned by 111_mcp_capabilities.sdoc. ActiveBlackboard behavior remains owned by 112_mcp_activeblackboard.sdoc. Internal subsystem semantics remain owned by their corresponding requirement files and existing implementation.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-MCP-PROMPT-ENGINEERING-TOOL
    9.1. TARGET Prompt-Engineering MCP Tool
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-MCP-PROMPT-ENGINEERING-TOOL
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-MCP-TOOL-PROTOCOL TARGET MCP Tool Operations
    RELATIONS (Child):

    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-MCP-CONFIG-PACKAGING TARGET MCP Prompt Configuration Packaging
    STATEMENT: The MCP server deployment shall include ghost_engineer_prompt as defined by 111_mcp_capabilities.sdoc.

    For each accepted invocation of that tool, the adapter shall create fresh request-isolated prompt state, reuse the existing deterministic PreProcessing path, then invoke the existing A2 PromptShaper path and return the resulting engineered prompt through the MCP result contract.

    This deployment requirement shall not redefine the functional scope of other MCP tools. Deterministic PreProcessing and A2 shall remain internal sequential stages of ghost_engineer_prompt and shall not be advertised as separate MCP tools unless separately approved.

    The deterministic prompt-construction step preceding A2 shall not call an LLM.

    GHOST-AWS-TGT-MCP-NO-EXTRA-TOOLS

    This deployment requirement shall not impose a prompt-engineering-only tool inventory. Standalone PreProcessing or standalone A2 tools shall remain excluded unless separately approved.

    The requirement set shall not prescribe an unverified library version.

    11. 11. TARGET Serverless EC2 Runtime Control

    STATEMENT: This section defines the AWS realization of the approved GHOST EC2 runtime-control capability.

    The controller is a small serverless control plane that remains reachable while the managed GHOST EC2 instance is stopped. It owns AWS-side start, stop, status, instance-profile selection, readiness verification, inactivity-state handling, and the redundant shutdown watchdog realization.

    The MCP-visible functional contract for these operations is owned by 113_mcp_runtime_control.sdoc.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL
    11.1. TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-DEPLOYMENT-CAPABILITY AWS Deployment and Operations Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-INDEPENDENT TARGET EC2-Independent Controller Endpoint
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-AUTH TARGET Runtime-Control Cognito Authentication
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-IAM TARGET Runtime-Control Least-Privilege IAM
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-PROFILES TARGET Selectable EC2 Runtime Profiles
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT TARGET Configurable Idle Timeout
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-START-SEQUENCE TARGET EC2 Start Sequence
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-STATUS TARGET EC2 Runtime Status Observation
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-STOP TARGET Explicit EC2 Stop
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-PROFILE-VALUES TARGET Runtime-Control Local Profile Values
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-ACCEPTANCE TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Acceptance
    STATEMENT: GHOST shall provide a serverless AWS control capability for the designated GHOST EC2 instance that can start the instance, report its runtime status, and stop the instance without depending on the EC2-hosted GHOST MCP server being available.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-INDEPENDENT
    11.2. TARGET EC2-Independent Controller Endpoint
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-INDEPENDENT
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: The runtime-control endpoint and its Lambda execution path shall remain available when the managed GHOST EC2 instance and all containers on that instance are stopped.

    The controller shall not require the EC2-hosted GHOST MCP endpoint in order to execute start, status, or stop operations.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-AUTH
    11.3. TARGET Runtime-Control Cognito Authentication
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-AUTH
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: The runtime-control endpoint shall require authenticated access through the existing approved GHOST Cognito identity environment. The existing approved GHOST Cognito user identity shall be usable for this controller and shall not require creation of a second end-user account.

    Unauthenticated requests shall not be permitted to start, stop, inspect, or reconfigure the managed EC2 instance.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-IAM
    11.4. TARGET Runtime-Control Least-Privilege IAM
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-IAM
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-FIXED-INSTANCE TARGET Fixed Managed EC2 Instance
    STATEMENT: The controller Lambda role shall receive only the permissions required for the approved runtime-control behavior.

    Start, stop, and instance-type modification permissions shall be restricted to the designated GHOST EC2 instance wherever AWS resource-level authorization permits it. Read-only describe permissions and access to the exact runtime-control SSM parameters may be broader only where required by AWS API semantics.

    The controller shall not receive EC2 termination permission.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-FIXED-INSTANCE
    11.5. TARGET Fixed Managed EC2 Instance
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-FIXED-INSTANCE
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-IAM TARGET Runtime-Control Least-Privilege IAM
    STATEMENT: The runtime controller shall operate only on the exact GHOST EC2 instance identifier recorded in the local deployment profile.

    The public MCP tool contract shall not accept an arbitrary EC2 instance identifier supplied by the caller.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-PROFILES
    11.6. TARGET Selectable EC2 Runtime Profiles
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-PROFILES
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-PROFILE-WHILE-STOPPED TARGET Instance-Type Selection While Stopped
    STATEMENT: The controller shall support exactly the following approved runtime profiles unless this requirement is later revised:

    1. Profile 1: t3.medium.
    2. Profile 2: m7i-flex.xlarge.

    Profile 1 shall be the default when the caller does not explicitly select a profile.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-PROFILE-WHILE-STOPPED
    11.7. TARGET Instance-Type Selection While Stopped
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-PROFILE-WHILE-STOPPED
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-PROFILES TARGET Selectable EC2 Runtime Profiles
    STATEMENT: The controller shall apply the selected EC2 instance type while the managed instance is in the stopped state and before issuing StartInstances.

    A start request received while the instance is not stopped shall not silently stop or restart the instance merely to change its instance type.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT
    11.8. TARGET Configurable Idle Timeout
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-STATE TARGET Lightweight Runtime-Control State
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-QUALIFYING-ACTIVITY TARGET Qualifying MCP Activity Definition
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LAMBDA-WATCHDOG TARGET Serverless Idle-Shutdown Watchdog
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG TARGET Independent EC2-Local Shutdown Watchdog
    STATEMENT: Each start operation shall establish one effective inactivity timeout for the resulting EC2 run.

    The default timeout shall be 20 minutes when the user does not provide a value.

    The effective timeout shall never be lower than 10 minutes or higher than 120 minutes. A requested value below 10 minutes shall be limited to 10 minutes, and a requested value above 120 minutes shall be limited to 120 minutes.

    The effective value shall be returned to the caller so the applied shutdown policy is visible.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-STATE
    11.9. TARGET Lightweight Runtime-Control State
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-STATE
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT TARGET Configurable Idle Timeout
    STATEMENT: The controller shall use the existing AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store service for the small non-secret runtime-control state required by the approved design.

    The state shall include at least the effective idle timeout and the latest qualifying MCP activity time needed by the serverless watchdog.

    Exact parameter names shall be recorded in the local deployment profile. No new database shall be required solely for this runtime-control capability.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-START-SEQUENCE
    11.10. TARGET EC2 Start Sequence
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-START-SEQUENCE
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-READINESS TARGET GHOST Readiness Verification
    STATEMENT: For an authenticated start request while the managed instance is stopped, the controller shall:

    1. resolve the requested runtime profile or use Profile 1 by default;
    2. resolve and constrain the requested idle timeout or use 20 minutes by default;
    3. modify the stopped instance to the selected approved EC2 type when necessary;
    4. persist the effective runtime-control state;
    5. initialize the run's last-activity time so an accidentally started but unused instance remains protected by the idle policy;
    6. issue StartInstances; and
    7. verify GHOST readiness before reporting the start operation as ready.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-READINESS
    11.11. TARGET GHOST Readiness Verification
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-READINESS
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-START-SEQUENCE TARGET EC2 Start Sequence
    STATEMENT: The controller shall not report GHOST as ready merely because the EC2 state is running.

    Readiness shall require a successful health check against the deployed GHOST service after the EC2 startup path, Docker activation, and public service path have become usable.

    The controller shall wait within one bounded start operation until readiness succeeds or the startup wait fails. A timeout or failed health check shall be reported as not ready and shall not be represented as successful readiness.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-STATUS
    11.12. TARGET EC2 Runtime Status Observation
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-STATUS
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: The controller shall be able to report the current EC2 state and, when available, the current approved runtime profile, concrete EC2 instance type, GHOST readiness state, effective idle timeout, and elapsed time since the latest qualifying MCP activity.

    A status observation shall not itself reset the GHOST inactivity timer.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-STOP
    11.13. TARGET Explicit EC2 Stop
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-STOP
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: An authenticated stop request shall stop the designated GHOST EC2 instance through the normal EC2 stop operation.

    The controller shall treat an already stopped instance safely and shall never translate the stop operation into instance termination.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-QUALIFYING-ACTIVITY
    11.14. TARGET Qualifying MCP Activity Definition
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-QUALIFYING-ACTIVITY
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT TARGET Configurable Idle Timeout
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-NON-ACTIVITY TARGET Background Traffic Does Not Prevent Shutdown
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-ACTIVITY-PUBLISH TARGET Dual Activity Recording
    STATEMENT: Only a real authenticated tools/call invocation accepted for execution by the EC2-hosted GHOST MCP service shall refresh the EC2 inactivity timer.

    Qualifying activity includes approved GHOST functional tool calls such as prompt engineering, retrieval, memory operations, and other authenticated GHOST MCP capabilities executed on the managed EC2 instance.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-NON-ACTIVITY
    11.15. TARGET Background Traffic Does Not Prevent Shutdown
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-NON-ACTIVITY
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-QUALIFYING-ACTIVITY TARGET Qualifying MCP Activity Definition
    STATEMENT: The inactivity timer shall not be refreshed by health checks, readiness polling, OAuth or discovery traffic, MCP initialization, tools/list, controller status polling, EventBridge or Lambda watchdog execution, Docker activity, operating-system activity, CPU usage, network background traffic, or other non-tools/call background behavior.

    The controller's own start, status, and readiness polling shall not create continuing GHOST activity after the initial start timestamp is established.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-ACTIVITY-PUBLISH
    11.16. TARGET Dual Activity Recording
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-ACTIVITY-PUBLISH
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-QUALIFYING-ACTIVITY TARGET Qualifying MCP Activity Definition
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-INFLIGHT-PROTECTION TARGET In-Flight MCP Call Protection
    STATEMENT: For each qualifying authenticated GHOST MCP tool call, the EC2-hosted MCP runtime shall refresh both:

    1. the serverless-visible last-activity value used by the Lambda watchdog; and
    2. a local last-activity marker used by the EC2-local watchdog.

    The implementation shall refresh activity when the call is accepted and again when the call completes so normal tool execution does not shorten the intended post-call idle period.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-INFLIGHT-PROTECTION
    11.17. TARGET In-Flight MCP Call Protection
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-INFLIGHT-PROTECTION
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-ACTIVITY-PUBLISH TARGET Dual Activity Recording
    STATEMENT: The inactivity watchdogs shall not stop the EC2 instance while a qualifying authenticated GHOST MCP tool call is actively executing.

    After the final active qualifying call completes, the effective idle timeout shall run from the refreshed completion activity time.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LAMBDA-WATCHDOG
    11.18. TARGET Serverless Idle-Shutdown Watchdog
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LAMBDA-WATCHDOG
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT TARGET Configurable Idle Timeout
    STATEMENT: A scheduled serverless watchdog shall check the managed EC2 runtime state at an interval no greater than one minute while applying the idle-shutdown policy.

    When the instance is running, no qualifying MCP call is active, and the elapsed time since the latest qualifying activity is at least the effective idle timeout, the watchdog shall issue StopInstances for the designated EC2 instance.

    When the instance is stopped, the watchdog shall perform no start or restart action.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG
    11.19. TARGET Independent EC2-Local Shutdown Watchdog
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-IDLE-TIMEOUT TARGET Configurable Idle Timeout
    RELATIONS (Child):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG-INDEPENDENCE TARGET Local Watchdog Independence and Stop Semantics
    STATEMENT: The EC2 host shall also run a lightweight local watchdog independent of the controller Lambda execution path.

    During boot, the host shall obtain the effective idle timeout established for the run and retain the value locally. The local watchdog shall evaluate the local qualifying-activity marker at an interval no greater than one minute.

    When no qualifying MCP call is active and the local inactivity duration reaches the effective timeout, the host shall initiate operating-system shutdown.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG-INDEPENDENCE
    11.20. TARGET Local Watchdog Independence and Stop Semantics
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG-INDEPENDENCE
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-LOCAL-WATCHDOG TARGET Independent EC2-Local Shutdown Watchdog
    STATEMENT: After boot initialization, the EC2-local watchdog shall not depend on successful execution of the controller Lambda in order to enforce inactivity shutdown.

    The managed EC2 instance's instance-initiated shutdown behavior shall be configured as stop rather than terminate so a local watchdog shutdown leaves the persistent EBS-backed instance available for later restart.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-PROFILE-VALUES
    11.21. TARGET Runtime-Control Local Profile Values
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-PROFILE-VALUES
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: Before deployment, the local profile shall record the exact managed EC2 instance identifier, controller endpoint value, Lambda function identity, Cognito values used by the controller, runtime-control SSM parameter names, scheduled-watchdog identity, local-watchdog activation artifact, readiness health URL, and any implementation-assigned startup wait limit.

    Secret values shall not be written into the requirement file or local profile.
    GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-ACCEPTANCE
    11.22. TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Acceptance
    UID: GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-CONTROL-ACCEPTANCE
    STATUS: Draft
    RELATIONS (Parent):
    • GHOST-AWS-TGT-EC2-RUNTIME-CONTROL TARGET EC2 Runtime-Control Capability
    STATEMENT: The runtime-control target shall not be promoted to CURRENT until acceptance demonstrates at least that:

    1. the controller remains reachable while the GHOST EC2 instance is stopped;
    2. unauthenticated control requests are rejected;
    3. start with omitted options uses Profile 1 t3.medium and a 20-minute idle timeout;
    4. Profile 2 starts the same stopped instance as m7i-flex.xlarge;
    5. the effective idle timeout cannot be configured below 10 or above 120 minutes;
    6. the start operation reports ready only after the GHOST health check succeeds;
    7. status reports the actual EC2 state without refreshing idle activity;
    8. explicit stop stops but does not terminate the instance;
    9. health checks, polling, and background host activity do not keep the instance alive;
    10. qualifying authenticated GHOST MCP tool calls refresh the inactivity timer;
    11. the serverless watchdog stops an idle instance; and
    12. the EC2-local watchdog independently stops an idle instance when the Lambda watchdog path is unavailable.
